title: The shifted finite-twist factor comparisons
statement: For any normalized positive finite-twist transport t and scheme morphism f with N invertible on its target, both prescribed shifted factor comparisons are the canonical inverse-image shift comparison followed by the shifted degree-zero single-object comparison. The positive comparison is at shift 2 and the negative comparison at shift -2.

source.place: The shifted finite-twist factor comparisons in the evaluation identification.

proof.text: Restrict the canonical signed transport to its roots and positive line. Its normalization makes this an OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport. Uniqueness identifies it with the supplied t. Thus the prescribed positive shifted comparison is the canonical signed comparison at twist 1 and shift 2. For it and the negative comparison at twist -1 and shift -2, unfold the common shifted comparison and identify its single-functor composite with singleFunctorPullbackMap.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteTwistShiftedFactorComparisons
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) :
    ((ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t f hY).hom =
      (((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).leftDerivedFunctor).commShiftIso (2 : ℤ)).hom.app
        (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA Y) ≫
        (singleFunctorPullbackMap (B := ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f
          (L := Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine Y N A hA)
          (L' := Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine X N A hA)
          (p1DecompositionSheafPullback A N hN hA f hY 1).hom)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧') ∧
    ((p1DecompositionTwistPullback A N hN hA f hY (-1) (-2)).hom =
      (((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).leftDerivedFunctor).commShiftIso (-2 : ℤ)).hom.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateSheaf A N Y hA (-1))) ≫
        (singleFunctorPullbackMap (B := ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f
          (p1DecompositionSheafPullback A N hN hA f hY (-1)).hom)⟦(-2 : ℤ)⟧')
